# MuSA (Multi-Source variant Annotation)

> Nextflow pipeline that turns a germline VCF (GRCh38) into one annotated row per variant (MAF)
> and a self-contained HTML report for rare-disease review. Published in BMC Bioinformatics
> (2026), doi:10.1186/s12859-026-06513-0. Current release: {{VERSION}}. Not a variant caller;
> runs after any caller.

Use MuSA when you need deep, reproducible annotation of germline small variants from a WES/WGS
VCF, a report a clinical geneticist can triage, or an analysis-ready table for statistics or
machine learning. Do not use it for GRCh37 input, somatic variants, SV/CNV calling or trio
inheritance analysis.

- Basic mode (default, ~30 GB, no registration, runs offline): Ensembl VEP, ClinVar (with review
  status and ClinGen expert-panel classifications), ClinGen gene-disease validity and dosage,
  offline HPO phenotype matching, ClinVar PS1/PM5 evidence. 168 columns.
- Extended mode (~200 GB): adds dbNSFP 5 (~35 predictors; academic registration), 32 VEP plugins
  (AlphaMissense, CADD, SpliceAI, SpliceVault, ProtVar, Gene2Phenotype, ...) and the RENOVO 1.5
  classifier. 887 columns.
- Optional online mode: ACMG/AMP scoring through the GeneBe API.
- Every database is pinned in a versioned manifest with SHA-256 checksums; 103 sources listed.
- Known limitations: SpliceAI SNV scores only; no gnomAD FAF95; no LOFTEE; no GIAB difficult-
  region flags; no trio analysis; GRCh38 only. Licence: CC BY-NC 4.0.

## Commands
- Setup (once): `nextflow run davide-scognamiglio/MuSA --workflow setup --data_dir $PWD/musa_data -profile docker`
- Annotate: `nextflow run davide-scognamiglio/MuSA --workflow annotate --input samplesheet.csv --outdir results --data_dir $PWD/musa_data -profile docker`
- Samplesheet columns: patient, sample_type, sample_file (VCF), hpo (optional, `;`-separated HPO IDs)

## Cite
Scognamiglio D, Bonetti E, Moroni A, Sangiorgi L, Pedrini E. MuSA: a Nextflow pipeline for deep,
reproducible annotation and clinical ranking of genomic variants. BMC Bioinformatics 27:199 (2026).
